# CANDIDATE: OPENING_RANGE_VOLUME_IMBALANCE_SHORT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Excess downside volume in the opening range predicts intraday weakness and a short bias. When down‑volume exceeds 1.5× up‑volume and price closes in the lower 20% of the opening range, a break below the opening‑range low offers a high‑probability short entry.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** In the first 30 minutes after the open, compute cumulative volume of down‑close bars (close < open) and up‑close bars (close ≥ open). If down‑volume / up‑volume ≥ 1.5 and the 30‑minute close is in the lower 20% of the opening‑range (high‑low) interval, place a stop order to enter short at a break below the opening‑range low. Only active when VIX > 18 and within the first 60 minutes after the open; skip if VIX < 15.  
**Exit:** Initial stop is chart‑stop at the opening‑range high. Take profit 1 at 1R (risk‑reward = 1). After TP1, trail the remaining position with a premium‑stop set at 20% of the ATR(14) (calculated on the 5‑minute chart).

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The strategy assumes a $25K+ account to trade the full qty (e.g., 28 contracts at ~$1.80 entry premium). A $1K paper account would realize roughly 14% of headline P&L due to the 50% per‑trade risk cap.
2. **Sample bias:** No historical sample has been evaluated yet; the proposal is based on a conceptual thesis. Any backtest would need to avoid look‑ahead bias by using only data available at the bar‑by‑bar level. Overfit risk is high until an out‑of‑sample test is performed.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk‑forward held‑out window has been run).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic OPRA simulation has been performed on the top three J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: a strong upward opening‑range break with high up‑volume could trigger a false short; max drawdown could exceed 50% of account if multiple false signals occur in a high‑VIX, trending‑up environment. Blow‑up scenario: persistent regime where down‑volume imbalance fails (e.g., low‑VIX chop) leading to repeated stop‑outs.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest (cannot estimate what fraction of P&L would come from the top‑5 days without historical results).

4 / 10 -- The hypothesis is intuitive but untested; volume‑imbalance signals are noisy and have not been validated on the OP‑16 anchor days. A Stage‑1 backtest is required to assess edge.

## Pre-existing leaderboard impact

This candidate does not conflict with any of the top‑9 leaderboard entries because it introduces a new short‑only trigger based on opening‑range volume imbalance, a dimension not covered by existing ORB‑related watchers (ORB_RETEST_LONG, ORB_NARROW_OR_GATE, ORB_DIRECTION_FILTER) or the quality gates currently deployed. It is complementary to existing volatility‑based filters (e.g., VIX > 18 condition) and could be combined with the existing chart‑stop exit logic.
